verdict_reason: The self-excluded cosine k-NN occurrence counts, population skewness, and Gini agree with independent formulas to machine precision. However, hubness_k*_top1pct is not the mass of exactly the top 1% under ties: 100 equal counts return 1.0 instead of 0.01.
comparable_reason: Skew/Gini are dimensionless but are not scale-free in the observed model population: across 42 models, vocab_size Spearman rho ranges from 0.322 to 0.508 for skew and 0.340 to 0.409 for Gini. A controlled Gaussian sweep at realistic widths found weak skew-width association (rho=0.092), but raw maximum occurrence retained a vocabulary-size effect (rho=0.625), so not every emitted field is cross-model comparable.
github_reason: No code release accompanying Radovanovic et al. 2010 or Tomasev et al. 2014 was located. The later third-party VarIr/scikit-hubness formula was inspectable but is not original-paper code; BLME's count-to-skew kernel nevertheless matched its scipy.stats.skew convention exactly on the shared occurrence fixture (2.1327252317535574).
paper_reason: Radovanovic et al. report S_N5=0.118 for 10,000 iid-normal points in 3-D under Euclidean distance. One hundred fresh stated-condition local replications averaged 0.115623 (2.014% relative error; SD 0.021593), placing the published realization only 0.11 SD away; the task's fixed cosine geometry cannot reproduce that Euclidean figure directly, and the paper gives no seed.
confounds_reason: In 42 archived model rows, k100 skew correlates with vocab_size at rho=0.508 (p=0.000599), while k10/k50/k100 maxima give rho=0.433/0.438/0.450. On 18 controlled Gaussian clouds spanning V=500-1000 and d=512-4096, max occurrence still correlates with V at rho=0.625; the canonical skew is much less mechanically width-sensitive (rho=0.092).
defects: src/blme/tasks/geometry/hubness.py:30-35 selects every count at or above a percentile threshold. For 100 tied counts of 10 it selects all 100 nodes and reports top1pct=1.0; an exact one-node top 1% has mass 0.01.

src/blme/tasks/geometry/hubness.py:112-123 leaves equal-similarity membership to torch.topk's arbitrary tie selection. Duplicate or highly quantized embeddings can therefore manufacture a device-dependent hub graph.

hubness_k*_max is an unnormalized extreme count: both model data and the controlled null show a vocabulary-size association, so it must not be treated as a beyond-scale feature without a size-matched null.
The provenance label says scikit-hubness parity, but no original-paper implementation was found; third-party formula agreement should not be presented as original-code parity.
fix: Compute top-1% mass from exactly m=ceil(0.01*V) largest occurrence counts with an explicit boundary-tie rule; use seeded or fractional membership for distance ties; and add a size-matched null-adjusted maximum while retaining the canonical raw skew/Gini outputs unchanged.
